A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GAGLE-based study. Text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable, and retained material can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original text-generation experiments, fractal measurements, prompting analyses and quality correlations, including Figures 3–10 and Tables 2–3.

after.justification: v2 retains these experiments and adds the authors' analysis of RAID texts, reported in Appendix A, Figures 11–14 and the expanded Table 3.

M1.justification: The generation procedures, prompting strategies and fractal-analysis method remain unchanged. Appendix B explains the existing estimators; RAID applies the same analytical approach to additional texts.

E1.justification: v2 adds RAID evaluation across abstracts, books, news, poetry, recipes, Reddit and reviews. Books, poetry, recipes and conversational/review material substantially broaden the original coverage of encyclopedic, patent, news, scientific and legal texts.

E2.justification: The compared diagnostics remain S, H and log-perplexity, with human text as the reference. RAID expands the generating models studied, but introduces no competing fractal estimator or detection baseline; existing GAGLE comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: The added RAID evaluation uses Gemini 1.0 Pro alone for scoring and displays temperatures 0 and 1. Prompts are uncontrolled, and Appendix A omits Q2/4/5/8. The original GAGLE preprocessing, temperature grid and evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A adds independent-corpus robustness checks of instruction-tuning and temperature effects, metric–quality relationships, and human/synthetic fractal distributions. Figures 11–14 test the generality of several central findings beyond GAGLE; the original prompting analyses and document case studies remain.

E5.justification: Both versions specify bootstrapping with replacement using 10 independent samples for confidence intervals and report correlations with p-values. RAID extends these reporting practices without documenting changed run counts, seeds or statistical procedures.

E6.justification: v2 adds seven RAID rows in Table 3 and results in Figures 11–14. RAID quality correlations are −0.67 for H and +0.21 for S, compared with retained GAGLE values of −0.71 and −0.25; these concern different corpora. GAGLE table changes are rounding, while some existing plotted error-bar bounds change slightly.

T1.justification: Appendix B supplies standard definitions and estimation formulas for the already-used fractal metrics, without introducing a new metric or theoretical result. Equations 1–3 remain unchanged, and the added Bayes-rule explanation elaborates the existing causal example.

C1.justification: The abstract and stated contributions retain the same claims about fractal differences, prompting, model generality, text quality and GAGLE. RAID supplies additional support for these claims without changing the central contribution or establishing a new detection capability.

C2.justification: v2 adds an explicit limitation concerning untested architectures such as state-space models and interprets the RAID poetry mismatch as particularly visible through S. It also discusses cross-corpus agreement, although the positive RAID S–quality correlation receives little qualification.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly documents the fractal-estimation calculations and identifies the previously published code used. Existing generation prompts, quality-rating instructions, GAGLE access information and data card are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to RAID, Tulchinskii et al.'s intrinsic-dimension detection work, and Mamba, while removing Willinger et al. (1995). These are limited extensions; the positioning around statistical characterization beyond perplexity remains.

P1.justification: The revision adds concise experimental and estimator appendices, expands the causal-example explanation, and makes localized wording and discussion edits. It corrects the reversed subset statement in Q7. The main nine-question structure and existing appendix content are preserved.

P2.justification: v2 adds RAID Figures 11–14 and divides the expanded Table 3 into GAGLE and RAID blocks. Tables relocate, model labels and captions are clarified, and Figure 4's incorrect top/middle/bottom references become left/center/right. Existing visual organization is largely retained.

improvement.justification: RAID provides useful external support for findings such as the Hurst–quality relationship, while estimator documentation and corrected captions improve clarity. The gain is bounded: RAID uses one scorer and omits four questions, and its positive S–quality correlation qualifies the claimed agreement without adequate discussion. Overall, the revision strengthens the paper without resolving its principal corpus-level and evaluation limitations.
